subtype: Approach: reward budget for small treats [Revision]
passage: My name is Yusuf. In February I decided to be strict with my first salary: no eating out, no small treats, nothing that wasn't a bill. For three weeks it worked perfectly. Then on the last Saturday I walked past a shop, saw a pair of headphones, and bought them without thinking, for far more than a treat should cost. I felt bad within an hour. Trisha listened to me over the phone and said, "You weren't weak, you were starved." She was right. So in March I added a line to the plan: a fun allowance of eight hundred a month, spent on anything I like. I was surprised how much easier the rest of the plan became.

qa.a: Yusuf bought a pair of headphones for far more than a treat should cost.

qa.q: How did Yusuf feel after buying the headphones?
qa.a: Yusuf felt guilty within an hour, though Trisha said it came from being starved of treats and not from weakness.

qa.q: What could Yusuf do if the fun allowance is spent in the first week, and why?
qa.a: Yusuf could divide it into weekly parts, since smaller portions make the treat last through the month.

qa.q: How might Trisha see the strict plan Yusuf started with?
qa.a: Trisha thought it was too strict, and probably worried that cutting out all fun would lead to a binge.

grounding: After a strict month ended in a binge purchase a person adds a small fun allowance to the plan, making the budget easier to keep.

Mentor's note, 28 February. Karthik, graduate-trainee mentor.
Dolma came to our fortnightly chat a little sheepish. In January she ran a very strict budget: no eating out, no shopping, not even tea at the stall downstairs. She was proud of it for three weeks. Then, on the last Saturday, she bought a ₹7,000 jacket and two pairs of shoes online in one evening, and the month ended worse than December.
'I don't know what happened,' she said. 'I was being so good.'
We talked it through. She decided on her own that February would include a ₹1,500 'fun line' for tea, one movie and small things, planned and guilt-free. Today she showed me: ₹1,340 used, no late-night shopping, and savings slightly up on January.
She laughed that the tea tasted better now that it was allowed. I'll ask about March at our next meeting.

qa.q: How much did Dolma set for the 'fun line' in February?
How did Dolma feel coming to the chat after January?
qa.a: She was sheepish and confused, since she felt she had been 'so good' and still ended the month worse.

qa.q: What would you suggest Dolma watch in March?
qa.a: Whether the fun line still feels like enough, adjusting it a little if cravings build again rather than going back to zero.

qa.q: How does the change look to Karthik, who wrote the note?
qa.a: Karthik sees the new plan working because Dolma chose it herself, and plans to follow up about March.

grounding: Shows a young earner whose strict month ended in a splurge, then adding a small planned fun allowance that makes the budget easier to keep.

passage:
Sunday, 3 November. Jyoti's diary.
Confession first. October was my 'zero fun' month. No cafés, no shopping, cooked every meal. I felt like a monk and was very proud of it.
Then on the 30th, after a horrible week at work, I bought wireless earbuds, a perfume and a hoodie, all at midnight. ₹6,200. More than I'd saved all month by being a monk.
Lokesh bhaiya laughed on the phone and said, 'You starved yourself and then ate the whole buffet.' Annoying, but true.
So November's plan has a new line: 'fun, ₹1,200'. Planned. Chai with Neelam on Fridays, one movie, maybe earrings. If it runs out, it runs out.
Weird to write 'fun' in a budget. It feels like permission. Maybe that's what I was missing.

qa.q: How much did the midnight shopping come to?
What does 'It feels like permission' suggest about how Jyoti feels?
qa.a: Jyoti feels relieved and lighter, as if planned treats remove the guilt that built up during the strict month.

qa.q: What else could help Jyoti after a horrible week at work?
qa.a: Having a small planned treat ready for such weeks, like the Friday chai, so stress doesn't turn into a midnight spree.

qa.q: How does Lokesh see Jyoti's October?
qa.a: Lokesh finds it funny but sees the pattern clearly: too strict a month led straight to a big splurge. 😅

grounding: Shows a young earner whose no-fun month ended in a midnight splurge, then planning a small fun allowance for the next month.
